title: A hymn in Prabhati
hookLine: Kabir's hymn in Prabhati starts with one light and ends with a question: so who is good, and who is bad?

lines: SO WHO IS GOOD, AND WHO IS BAD?
A QUESTION THAT BEGINS WITH LIGHT.
cards: So who is good, and who is bad? People ask it about strangers on the news, the neighbors, the driver who just cut in, usually with an answer already waiting.
In the Prabhati section of the Guru Granth Sahib, the Bhagat Kabir asks it too, in a hymn the Gurus placed among their own.
But he asks it at the end of a sentence that begins with light, and by the time the question arrives, a ready answer may not fit.

teach.h: FROM ONE LIGHT, THE WHOLE WORLD.
teach.b: Here's the opening, in paraphrase. First, God brought forth the light, and from that power came all people. From one light the whole world sprang up.

So who is good, and who is bad? Kabir uses the name Allah here, and the word noor for light; in other hymns he calls the One Ram, among other names. Then the Rahao: people, don't wander lost in doubt.
The Creator is in the creation, and the creation is in the Creator, filling every place. Then Kabir picks up a pot.
The clay is one; the Maker shaped it in many ways. There's no fault in the clay pots, and no fault in the potter. The One is in everything, and all of it happens by the Maker's doing.
Whoever recognizes the Maker's will, the hukam, knows the One. The hymn closes with Kabir himself: the Guru gave him something sweet, his fear went, and he sees the Pure One everywhere.
Set that at daybreak, where tradition sings Prabhati.
Dawn light doesn't pick. It reaches the dome of the gurdwara and the alley behind it, the person you love and the person you can't stand.

If everyone is clay from one pit, shaped by one hand, lit by one light, then good and bad stop being two kinds of people. The hymn doesn't say no one does wrong. It says no one is made of different stuff.

how: Kabir's hymn of the one light is sung in kirtan in Raga Prabhati and is sometimes quoted when Sikhs speak of the equality of all people.

games.q: what does “a hymn in prabhati” mean?
o: Kabir's song: from one light came all, so who is good or bad?
a hymn about the potter's trade and village crafts
Guru Nanak's list of morning duties for a household

games.q: what's inside Kabir's hymn — tap the pairs.
p: the Creator is in the creation

s: Kabir's hymn says no one ever does wrong
it says everyone is made from one light and one clay; it doesn't deny wrongdoing.
the hymn finds no fault in the clay pots or the potter
the clay is one, and the Maker shaped it in many ways.

games.q: you're Kabir. you've just sung that the whole world sprang from one light. what comes next in your line?
o: so the good must be rewarded.
so who is good, and who is bad?
so stay away from the bad.
games.why: the hymn asks the question right after the light: if all came from one light, who is good, and who is bad?

practice: If you can, play Kabir's hymn of the one light, or another shabad sung in Prabhati; if not, sit in the quiet.

Let the breath go out toward one person you love, then one you hardly know, whoever delivered your last parcel, then, gently, someone you find hard, the same breath and the same light reaching all three, the way morning reaches every street.
If you pray, remember the one light Kabir names; if you don't, simply notice the three faces side by side.

wordCard.voice: A hymn in Prabhati. Kabir's song that from one light the whole world sprang up, one clay shaped into many pots, so who is good, and who is bad? Today's word.

orig.note: light: Kabir's word in Prabhati for the one light the world sprang from.

carryVoice: Your line: light at dawn. One clay, many pots, and one light on all of them. Thanks for sitting with me.

sources.ref: Prabhati, Bani Bhagat Kabir, 'Aval Allah noor upaia', Ang 1349
